```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: FALSE

library("knitr")
library("xml2")
library("magick")
library("kableExtra")
```

# Background and aim
Mental health problems are prevalent in children with disabilities. Many studies have focused on identifying predictors that are relatively non-modifiable, such as age and parental education. However, for the purpose of developing psychological and pedagogical interventions, identifying potentially modifiable factors, such as participation, may be more important. Further, predictors of mental health problems may differ between children with and without disabilities, potentially informing the adaptation of interventions for different disability groups. This study aims to investigate differences in predictors of mental health problems between children and adolescents with and without disabilities.

# Methods
The study uses a cross-sectional design to analyse data from different cohorts collected between 2013 and 2019 through the Swedish Child Living Conditions Survey (BarnULF) and the linked survey on Living Conditions (ULF/SILC). BarnULF is an annual interview-based survey of children aged 10–18 years, linked to information provided by their participating caregivers (in ULF/SILC), that is administered by Statistics Sweden (SCB). The survey include questions about everyday experiences, including school, leisure activities, family, firends, and mental health.

## Data analysis
LASSO regression was used to identify predictors of mental health problems separately across five disability groups and a group of children without disabilities. For each group, 28 variables were entered into the models as candidate predictors. Predictors were standardized, and the penalty parameter was selected using cross-validation, with the one-standard-error rule ($\lambda_{\text{1se}}$) used to favour a more parsimonious model.

## LASSO

@fig-lasso-paths show how predictor coefficients change as the regularization parameter ($\lambda$) increases across the five impairment groups and the group with neurotypical children. Increasing regularization shrinks coefficients towards zero, with the selected value of($\lambda$) (indicated by the dashed vertical line) reflecting the chosen degree of penalization. The figures illustrate differences in which predictors are retained and the magnitude and direction of their coefficients across groups.

```{r}
#| include: FALSE
#| label: combine-path-figures
# Locate the six LASSO coefficient-path plots
plot_files <- sort(
  list.files(
    "output",
    pattern = "^lasso_paths_.*\\.png$",
    full.names = TRUE
  )
)

# Exclude the previously generated combined image
plot_files <- plot_files[
  basename(plot_files) != "lasso_paths_combined.png"
]

stopifnot(length(plot_files) == 6)

# Read the six plots at their original resolution
plots <- lapply(plot_files, magick::image_read)

# Combine into a 2-column by 3-row grid
combined <- magick::image_montage(
  magick::image_join(plots),
  tile = "2x3",
  geometry = "+10+10"
) |>
  magick::image_background("white")

# Save the combined figure
magick::image_write(
  combined,
  path = "output/lasso_paths_combined.png",
  format = "png"
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-lasso-paths
#| fig-cap: "LASSO coefficient paths by group"
#| fig-alt: "Six panels showing how estimated coefficients change as the regularization parameter varies."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 12

knitr::include_graphics("output/lasso_paths_combined.png")
```

Across the six groups, the LASSO models showed broadly similar coefficient patterns (see @tbl-lasso-coefficients). Child age, child sex, family relationships, and having a single parent had negative coefficients, whereas parent anxiety had a positive coefficient.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-lasso-coefficients
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "LASSO coefficients by group"
# Load the saved LASSO results
lasso_results <- readRDS("data/lasso_results.rds")

# Define the six groups in the desired order
groups <- c(
  "td",
  "asthma_allergy",
  "adhd_asd",
  "dyslexia_dyscalculia",
  "other_broader",
  "sensory"
)

# Extract coefficients from each model
coefficient_list <- lapply(groups, function(group) {
  coefficients <- as.matrix(lasso_results[[group]]$coefficients)[, 1]
  coefficients
})

names(coefficient_list) <- groups

# Collect all predictor names across the six models
predictors <- sort(unique(unlist(
  lapply(coefficient_list, names)
)))

# Exclude the intercept
predictors <- setdiff(predictors, "(Intercept)")

# Create a wide table, using zero for coefficients not selected
# by a particular LASSO model
coefficient_table <- data.frame(
  Predictor = predictors,
  do.call(
    cbind,
    lapply(coefficient_list, function(x) {
      values <- x[predictors]
      values[is.na(values)] <- 0
      as.numeric(values)
    })
  ),
  check.names = FALSE
)

names(coefficient_table) <- c("Predictor", groups)

# Replace zero coefficients with NA
coefficient_table[-1] <- lapply(
  coefficient_table[-1],
  function(x) {
    x[x == 0] <- NA_real_
    x
  }
)

# Remove rows where all six coefficients are NA
coefficient_table <- coefficient_table[
  rowSums(!is.na(coefficient_table[-1])) > 0,
]

# Create the table
coefficient_table %>%
  kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 3,
    align = c("l", rep("c", ncol(coefficient_table) - 1)),
    escape = TRUE,
    na = "",
    row.names = FALSE
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = NULL,
    full_width = FALSE,
    position = "left"
  ) %>%
  row_spec(
    0,
    bold = TRUE,
    extra_css = "border-top: 1px solid black; border-bottom: 1px solid black;"
  ) %>%
  row_spec(
    nrow(coefficient_table),
    extra_css = "border-bottom: 1px solid black;"
  )
```
